 Asean (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) Apec and Asean summits live: protests await Trump in Manila, as Xi greets leaders in Shenzhen
 US president flies into Asean summit amid protests over the US-led Pax Silica initiative on AI and critical minerals as Apec meeting underway in China
 Xi, Trump and Putin to discuss ‘world peace’ at trilateral, says China 
 What is Apec? - explained in 30 seconds

 Indigenous people from the Cordillera region hold a protest at Bonifacio Park in Manila, condemning US President Donald Trump's visit to the Philippines Photograph: Charles Edmon S Perez/JNA/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen Indigenous people from the Cordillera region hold a protest at Bonifacio Park in Manila, condemning US President Donald Trump's visit to the Philippines Photograph: Charles Edmon S Perez/JNA/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock Yohannes Lowe (now) and Mark Saunokonoko (earlier) Tue 17 Nov 2026 04.10 EST First published on Mon 16 Nov 2026 20.00 EST Share From 2h ago 02.01 EST Interim summary
 It has just gone 3pm in Manila (host to the Asean summit) and Shenzhen (Apec). Here’s the main news from both cities so far today. There is plenty more to come so stay with us.
 China will ⁠cut $280m in tariffs on Canadian ​exports including pork and seafood , Mark Carney’s office said after he met with Xi Jinping. Carney hailed “greater predictability and stability” in China-Canada relations.
 Canada and ​China also agreed to extend by two years ⁠existing remission measures for certain ​Chinese ​steel and ​aluminium products .
 Papua ⁠New Guinea’s prime minister James Marape ⁠confirmed that Taiwan does not operate in ⁠the Pacific country anymore , during a meeting ⁠with Xi ​in Shenzhen. “We hope this assists you in your efforts for reunification,” Marape added.
 Donald Trump is flying on the new Air Force One, gifted to him by Qatar, to Manila where a meeting with Quad leaders is scheduled for later today.
 Japan ⁠has proposed creating a task force to coordinate cooperation in Asia on oil stockpiling and the release of supplies during emergencies – ⁠one that will allow ⁠neighbours ​in the region to use idle storage capacity in Japan.

 18m ago 04.10 EST During a ​meeting with Xi Jinping , Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum said ⁠that her country wanted to strengthen ​cooperation with ‌China in ‌areas related ‌to technology, agriculture, water resources, health and tourism.
 The two leaders were speaking in the southern ​Chinese tech and manufacturing hub of ⁠Shenzhen ahead of ​the two-day Apec economic summit which starts tomorrow.
 View image in fullscreen Mexico’s President Claudia Sheinbaum (L) speaks as her foreign minister Roberto Velasco Alvarez (R) looks on during a bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Photograph: Maxim Shemetov/EPA Share 55m ago 03.32 EST As we mentioned in a previous post , hundreds of people have been arrested in heated demonstrations against the arrival of Donald Trump in Manila (expected in an hour or so), with many protesters angry at the new US-led Pax Silica initiative on AI and critical minerals.
 The Guardian Australia’s political editor, Tom McIlroy , explains why so many people are rejecting the initiative and provides some details about what it entails: 
 Pax Silica has sparked tensions in the Philippines over plans to build a tech hub outside Manila that critics say will affect water and energy supplies, and displace members of the Ayta Indigenous community.
 Pax Silica will include a technology hub planned at New Clark City in Tarlac, about 120km from Manila.
 Intended to bolster western stocks of AI technology and reduce “excessive dependencies” on single source supply chains, including from China, Pax Silica will provide chips and critical minerals to 25 participating signatory governments.
 View image in fullscreen Indigenous people from the Cordillera region hold a protest at Bonifacio Park in Manila, condemning Trump's upcoming visit to the Philippines for the Asean summit. Photograph: Charles Edmon S Perez/JNA/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock Share 2h ago 02.54 EST The Philippines president, Ferdinand Marcos Jr , has called for concrete safeguards for food and energy supplies across south east Asia and east Asia in order to protect households and businesses from higher prices caused by global supply disruptions.
 He said the impact of conflicts (such as the US-Israel war on Iran) has caused prices and energy costs to rise across the region, hitting consumers hard.
 “A disruption thousands of miles away can reach households across east and southeast Asia through the price of rice, the cost of energy, or the loss of a day’s income,” Marcos Jr was quoted as having said. The Philippines president said it is imperative to keep maritime trade and logistics moving and secure essential supplies to withstand shocks.
 “Our task today is to put our collective strength to work. In ships reaching their destinations, in reliable supplies of food and energy, in businesses continuing to operate, and in families facing the future with greater confidence,” he said.
 View image in fullscreen Ferdinand Marcos Jr (C) speaks on the sidelines of the Asean Summit on 17 November 2026 in Manila, the Philippines. Photograph: Jam Sta Rosa/Pool/Getty Images Share Updated at  03.02 EST 2h ago 02.16 EST China is hosting the summit for the third time, after Shanghai (2001) and Beijing (2014). Both domestic ​and international reasons govern the choice of Shenzhen, said Chim Lee, ‌senior analyst at the Economist Intelligence Unit.
 As part of China’s Greater Bay Area home to Hong Kong and Macau, which Beijing seeks to establish ‌as a global hub for technology and innovation, the city offers a platform to showcase China’s vision for development and trade.
 It also highlights Shenzhen’s resilience to geopolitical turbulence, Lee added. Shenzhen is the base for several Chinese auto and tech companies, such as BYD, Huawei and Tencent.
 View image in fullscreen A delivery man rides past a sign promoting Apec in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, China. Photograph: Ng Han Guan/AP Share 2h ago 02.08 EST France and Malaysia agree series of deals, including rare earths
 France and Malaysia upgraded bilateral ⁠ties to a strategic ⁠partnership and ​announced a slew of cooperation deals today , with Kuala Lumpur agreeing to relax export curbs on raw rare earths to support joint development in ⁠the sector.
 The announcement came following a meeting between French president Emmanuel Macron and Malaysia’s prime minister Anwar Ibrahim in Kuala Lumpur. Macron is on a two-day visit ​to Malaysia, his first since 2017.
 View image in fullscreen Emmanuel Macron attends a meeting with Anwar Ibrahim in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. Photograph: Fazry Ismail/POOL EPA/AP “This renewed partnership will contribute to strengthen our independence on both sides,” ‌Macron said, adding it would also boost the two countries’ defence and security.
 Anwar said Malaysia has agreed to export some raw rare earths materials to France following a commitment by Paris to collaborate on rare earths processing.

 It has just gone 3pm in Manila (host to the Asean summit) and Shenzhen (Apec). Here’s the main news from both cities so far today. There is plenty more to come so stay with us.
 China will ⁠cut $280m in tariffs on Canadian ​exports including pork and seafood , Mark Carney’s office said after he met with Xi Jinping. Carney hailed “greater predictability and stability” in China-Canada relations.
 Canada and ​China also agreed to extend by two years ⁠existing remission measures for certain ​Chinese ​steel and ​aluminium products .
 Papua ⁠New Guinea’s prime minister James Marape ⁠confirmed that Taiwan does not operate in ⁠the Pacific country anymore , during a meeting ⁠with Xi ​in Shenzhen. “We hope this assists you in your efforts for reunification,” Marape added.
 Donald Trump is flying on the new Air Force One, gifted to him by Qatar, to Manila where a meeting with Quad leaders is scheduled for later today.
 Japan ⁠has proposed creating a task force to coordinate cooperation in Asia on oil stockpiling and the release of supplies during emergencies – ⁠one that will allow ⁠neighbours ​in the region to use idle storage capacity in Japan.
 Share 3h ago 01.57 EST Coming back to those comments we flagged earlier from the BYD chairman Wang Chuanfu at the Apec CEO summit .
 Wang said BYD depends on local ⁠supply ⁠chains for ​most of ⁠its procurement in some overseas regions ⁠including ​in ‌ Thailand . Between 90% and ​95% of employees at the ⁠carmaker’s plants in Brazil ​and ​ Chile are ​locally ​hired, ‌he said.
 Share 3h ago 01.45 EST And those protests in Manila awaiting Trump ?
 Tom McIlroy is on the ground in Manila and he has just filed this story . He writes that organisers claim as many as 10,000 people will join the anti-Trump protests today . Hundreds of people have been arrested so far.
 Here’s some video from the protests.
 0:54 ‘Not welcome here’: Filipinos protest ahead of Trump’s visit to Manila for Asean summit – video Share Updated at  01.53 EST 3h ago 01.37 EST What's on Trump's Tuesday agenda in Manila?
 If you’re just joining us, Trump is expected to land in Manila soon. He is flying in on the new Air Force One , gifted to him by the Qataris.
 Shortly after the US president arrives in the Philippines, he heads to a meeting with the leaders of the Quad , a group of nations including the US , Australia , India and Japan that has aimed to counter China ’s influence in the Asia Pacific . Trump is then scheduled to sign a trade deal with Thailand .
 Before a dinner on Tuesday night, Trump will participate in what’s billed as a “special summit” with the Asean leaders , where they are expected to discuss efforts to deepen trade and security ties as well as the region’s longstanding conflicts, including Myanmar and the South China Sea , which Beijing claims virtually in its entirety.
 Trump is also expected to announce a series of commercial deals and investments in the aviation, defence, energy, and technology sectors, before heading to Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit .

 Allow and continue Share Updated at  03.10 EST 3h ago 01.28 EST The chair of Chinese EV manufacturer BYD, Wang Chuanfu, is making some remarks at Apec . We’ll bring you the top news lines as they come in.
 Share 3h ago 01.24 EST The question of the Apec “family photo” and who may or may not object to lining up alongside Putin certainly is pertinent. 
 Last month at the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in the US , the traditional “family photo” was abruptly cancelled after a host of nations – including the UK and Australia – refused to appear beside the Russian foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov .
 Will we see a similar scenario unfold in Shenzhen?
 Share 3h ago 01.15 EST Australia’s prime minister, Anthony Albanese, says he welcomes the forthcoming Trump-Xi-Putin summit , despite reservations from some European leaders. More on Albanese’s thoughts here .
 Interestingly, when asked on Sunday if he would join the so-called “family photo” of Apec leaders if Putin took part , Albanese said he would consider the wishes of China as the host nation.
 But Albanese said Putin should know Australia’s opposition to the invasion, adding:
 double quotation mark If he’s in a room where I am, I’m sure they’ll hear my contribution.”
 Albanese is in Manila right now, where he awaits the arrival of Donald Trump for a Quad leaders. meeting . The Australian prime minister will head for Apec in China after Manila.
 Share Updated at  01.20 EST 4h ago 00.55 EST While we’re on the subject of Russia, analysts say the main beneficiary of the Trump-Xi-Putin meeting set for later this week is likely Putin .
 They say Putin’s standing will be boosted by being treated on an equal footing by two other leaders whose countries are, in reality, much more powerful.
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Pavel Bednyakov,brendan Smialowski,maxim Shemetov/AFP/Getty Images Despite that, Lyle Goldstein , a China specialist at Brown University, said the meeting was unlikely to bring about any substantive results.
 double quotation mark There will be no ‘Yalta’, as many have feared. 
 And Jonathan Czin , from the Brookings Institution, cautioned that Trump’s lame duck status would deter Xi and Putin from trying to reach long-term arrangements with the US.
 “Both men know Trump’s time is expiring even more quickly than his leverage – and that he will be irrelevant in a mere 26 months [when his term expires],” Cain told an online Brookings forum .
 double quotation mark Why would either man make a deal with a leader whose time and leverage are waning? They will only do it if they think they can pilfer more from Trump diplomatically than they will be able to gain from the next American president. 
 Share Updated at  02.12 EST 4h ago 00.52 EST Japan said it scrambled fighter jets today after suspected Russian aircraft violated its airspace, prompting Tokyo to lodge a protest with Moscow in a further deterioration of relations between the two nations. 
 The two “suspected Russian” planes entered Japan’s airspace close to Okinoshima, in the south-western area of Fukuoka, shortly after 4am Tuesday, top government spokesman Minoru Kihara said.
 Japanese prime minister Sanae Takaichi (currently in Manila for Asean) and Russian president Vladimir Putin are both due at the Apec summit in Shenzhen this week.
 Share Updated at  01.03 EST 4h ago 00.35 EST Elon Musk will travel with Trump to China 
 When Trump (who is currently on Air Force One flying to Manila for Asean ) flies to Shenzhen in China for Apec , he will be accompanied by Elon Musk , White House officials have confirmed.
 The reason for Musk’s presence has not been explained. But the Tesla and SpaceX boss spent $500m supporting unsuccessful Republican candidates in this month’s midterms. You can read more about that failed cash injection here .
 View image in fullscreen Donald Trump and Elon Musk in 2024. Photograph: Brandon Bell/Reuters Elon Musk’s nearly half a billion dollars in midterms spending was a flop Read more Share 4h ago 00.26 EST We have some more detail on that meeting between Xi and Papua New Guinea’s prime minister James Marape , including those remarks on Taiwan we reported on earlier.
 Marape said the effort to turn away from Taiwan wasn’t easy: “I faced challenges from within, because we also relate to many nations, but we ⁠were resolved.”
 He added: “China respects the sovereignty of Papua New ​Guinea. We must give ​full respect for the ​sovereignty of China.”
 In response, Xi said China is ​willing to ‌work with Papua ​New Guinea ​to deepen political mutual trust, consolidate and expand mutually beneficial cooperation in various fields.
 In early November, Taiwan said ⁠it had decided to shut its representative office in Papua New Guinea and stop buying liquefied natural gas ⁠from the country, blaming Chinese pressure. Papua New Guinea briefly had diplomatic ​relations with Taipei in 1999 ‌before restoring ties ‌with China.
